note: foam wedges on all four walls, carpeted floor, acoustic tile ceiling; RT60 0.14 s (paper, Table 1); base, rotated and translated loudspeaker, and one whiteboard panel directly in front of the loudspeaker (condition Panel; paper Appendix C.1)

label: Hallway (Stanford University)
note: narrow reverberant hallway, two wooden doors, tile floor, drywall walls and ceiling; RT60 1.41 s averaged over frequencies (paper, Table 1); base, rotated and translated loudspeaker, and three whiteboard-panel conditions (Panel1 in front of the loudspeaker at a slant, Panel2 behind it, Panel3 both). The paper's 1.41 s is an average over frequencies; the hallway's decay peaks at mid frequencies (T30 0.94 s at 125 Hz, 2.3 s at 500 Hz-1 kHz, 0.94 s at 8 kHz), so RIRDB's 500 Hz-1 kHz value is 2.3 s; averaged over 63 Hz-8 kHz it is 1.6 s.
